definitions.meaning: a formal assembly or conference of delegates
an old formal word for sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: An invitation to a gathering whose real purpose is rather less businesslike.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a formal assembly and, in an older sense, sexual union.

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Holding back a policeman who happens to be extremely powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol; 'very strong' is the music direction fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff someone is to restrain them, and the short verb form means the same.

indicators.note: being caught by something means being held inside it

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing, nil
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone's clothing snagged in a zipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' puts A inside NIL; 'zip' means nothing, not the fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A small metal spike hammered in to fix things together is a common fastener.

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
to heel is to tip or lean over, said of a ship

explanation.surface: Mending shoes, perhaps for a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler fixing worn shoes fits a new back part to the sole, which is exactly this repair.

clue.text: Firm with year contracts, over time they stop firing

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed over another sits above it, so time comes before year

parts.note: firm, as in secure, means safe
to contract an illness is to catch it

explanation.surface: A company signing annual deals that run out over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts T above Y in the down entry; 'Firm' is a company in the surface but means secure.
explanation.definitionFit: The locks on guns that prevent accidental discharge are these safety devices.

clue.text: Carriage clock's second hand initially missing gold

indicators.note: the second letter of the word clock is picked
the word hand loses its opening letter

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A carriage clock whose second hand has lost its gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage clock' and 'second hand' are false phrases: 'second' picks L from clock, and 'initially missing' takes H off hand, leaving AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with a folding top is a type of carriage.

clue.text: Piano playing with the short new song

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played about with, rearranged
short means the word the loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A pianist accompanying a brief new song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges PIANO with TH ('the' made 'short') into ANTIPHO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hymn or chant sung in alternate parts by two choirs, so a kind of song.

clue.text: Fancy dress? Endless fun around large party city

indicators.note: around means the anagram goes round the following letters
fancy here means elaborately reworked, signalling a rearrangement
endless means the word fun loses its last letter

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A fancy-dress party where the fun runs out, around a big celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' makes DUSSERF from the costume word plus FU ('Endless' fun), and 'around' splits it after the fifth letter; the city's umlaut is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large German city on the Rhine, capital of North Rhine-Westphalia.

clue.text: Winning team drink in complete confusion

parts.note: a player who is up is ahead, winning
a side is a team
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: The victorious team celebrate with drinks and end up in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned topsy-turvy is in total disorder, an idiomatic sense of the phrase.

parts.note: just, meaning fair and deserved, is rightful

explanation.surface: A man who is simply disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like an adverb meaning simply, but it is the adjective fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or appalling is revolting, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Breaking ice with him: full bar providing drink

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters being broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Breaking the ice with a man at a crowded bar by offering a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges the thirteen letters of ICE, HIM and FULL BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet white German wine, so a drink.

definitions.meaning: trials or attempts to see if something works
full cricket or rugby games between national sides

explanation.surface: Rugby scores appearing in games between countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like rugby scores but means attempts or trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Trials are attempts, and the same word names full matches between countries in cricket and rugby.

parts.note: the eye of a storm or target is its centre
to spread something is to cover a surface with it

explanation.surface: An eye patch with a picture showing what lies beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle double page of a magazine, often carrying a racy photo, is a revealing image.

clue.text: Clubs topping alcoholic drink with finest fruit

indicators.note: topping means the clubs letter replaces the head of the drink

parts.note: sherry is a fortified wine
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a plum job or role is the best, finest one

explanation.surface: Clubs crowning a fine drink with the best fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' puts C in place of the first letter of SHERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cherry-like plum from the myrobalan tree is a fruit.

parts.note: pornographic means dirty or smutty
linen is a fabric, a material

explanation.surface: Someone's private dealings involve smut.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for personal matters best kept from public view, as in airing them in public.

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A stage show featuring a difficult number.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the famous 1960s rock musical about hippies.

clue.text: Made platform sole comfortable, although, primarily foot collapsed

indicators.note: primarily means the opening letter of each of the four words is taken

parts.note: something collapsed has folded

explanation.surface: A shoe platform felt comfortable, though the foot gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made platform' sounds like shoemaking but means erected a framework of poles and planks.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting up a temporary structure of poles and boards to work from is erecting a platform.

definitions.meaning: long loose knickers worn by women
slips in the sense of blunders or mistakes

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some undergarments are petticoats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' looks like more underwear, but here means errors.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names baggy women's knickers and, in British slang, embarrassing mistakes.

clue.text: This could be an old bus conductor's role in retirement?

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Wondering what part a former bus conductor might play once retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests a bus but names the orchestral conductor Simon Rattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickety, noisy old vehicle is called this, so an old bus could be one.

indicators.note: on means the line comes next to, following, the book

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: The heading line written on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The crest or summit of a hill is called its brow, so it means the top.

clue.text: One rents large spaces everywhere, all empty

indicators.note: each of the three words is emptied of its inner letters, leaving just its ends

explanation.surface: A tenant takes huge spaces all over, all of them vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all empty' leaves LE, SS and EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holding a lease is the person who rents the property.

parts.note: yellow is a colour
to hammer metal is to shape it

explanation.surface: Colour and form chosen for festive flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunting' suggests flags but is the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: This songbird with a yellow head is a member of the bunting family.

parts.note: par means the usual or normal level

explanation.surface: Juvenile fish taken from the normal stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A young salmon before it goes to sea is given this name.

parts.note: Team Sky was a British professional cycling team

explanation.surface: A bike racing squad on holiday on an island in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an island of the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

indicators.note: in means the caught letter sits inside the channel word

parts.note: a lane is a channel or passage, as a shipping lane
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A small fish netted in the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The small burrowing fish also called a sand lance is a type of eel-like fish.

clue.text: Pitch in Rugby Union town to go after game

parts.note: Sale, near Manchester, is home to the rugby union club Sale Sharks
to stalk is to pursue game animals

explanation.surface: A rugby ground in a town where people go hunting after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a playing field but means a sales patter.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasive patter used to sell something is a pitch.

clue.text: One believer is gripped by second part of bible

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: being gripped by something means being held inside it

parts.note: NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A believer who is clutched by the latter half of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One believer' is a single fused definition: someone believing reality is one substance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a philosopher holding that reality is made of a single substance, a believer in oneness.

indicators.note: put straight means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A device where toes are set right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put straight' rearranges HERE TOES; the whole clue also describes the device.
explanation.definitionFit: This shoe-shaped insert keeps footwear in shape, straightening the toe area.
